**Finding submitted: `missing` (critical), confidence 0.95**

## What I found

The Agreement has **no indemnification provision whatsoever**. The section outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) directly to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability) — Section 20 simply does not exist. I confirmed this by searching for "indemnif", "hold harmless", "defend", and "infring": the only three hits are incidental references, not operative indemnity language.

Critically, the rest of the document **assumes Section 20 exists**, leaving dangling cross-references:

- **§ 9.3** conditions Customer's termination right on Vendor's inability to provide "the remedies required by Section 20.5"
- **§ 19.4** preserves remedies for "indemnified claims"
- **§ 21.3** makes "its indemnification obligations" an Excluded Claim
- **§ 30.5** grants enforcement rights to an "indemnified party" and protects "vested indemnity rights"

This sits at the playbook's walk-away line (no Vendor IP indemnity at all), so I went to the **preferred** position rather than fallback.

## The redline (validated `ok:true`)

Inserted a new Section 20 after § 19.5, immediately before Limitation of Liability:

- **20.1** — Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer **and its Affiliates** for (a) IP infringement by Services, Deliverables or Vendor Technology; (b) breach of Applicable Law; (c) Vendor-caused unauthorized access to Customer Data; (d) gross negligence/wilful misconduct
- **20.2** — Customer's indemnity kept **narrow**: only Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, with an express "no other indemnification obligation" backstop
- **20.3** — Standard procedure (notice with materiality-of-prejudice qualifier, control, cooperation, settlement consent)
- **20.4** — Customary IP exclusions (modifications, combinations, Customer specifications)
- **20.5** — Procure/modify/replace/refund remedies — which also **repairs the § 9.3 cross-reference**

## Drafting judgments worth flagging

I used defined terms already in the document (Affiliates, Deliverables, Vendor Technology, Customer Data, Applicable Law, Order Form, Fees) so the new section integrates without new definitions.

I deliberately **did not add a 3× annual fees super-cap** from the fallback. § 21.3 already carves indemnification obligations out of the liability cap entirely, so importing a super-cap would have *reduced* our recovery below the existing bargain. I also numbered the remedies clause as 20.5 specifically to match the § 9.3 reference, which is why the customary exclusions sit at 20.4.

One note for your negotiation: this document shows signs of other one-sided or anomalous terms nearby (e.g. duplicate § 7.2 and § 12.4 paragraphs, a Singapore governing-law clause at § 28.1 conflicting with New York jurisdiction at § 28.2). Those fall outside this rule, but they suggest the draft merits a broader review.
